Convert between neuroim2 objects and RNifti / oro.nifti images

Source: R/interop.R
as_neuro.Rd

as_neuro() turns an image held by another R neuroimaging package into a neuroim2 object, and as_nifti() goes the other way. Together they let neuroim2 take part in a pipeline built on RNifti, RNiftyReg, oro.nifti, neurobase or fslr without a round trip through a file.

Usage

as_neuro(x, ..., label = "")

as_nifti(x, xform_code = 1L)

# S3 method for class 'NeuroObj'
asNifti(x, reference = NULL, ..., xform_code = 1L)

Arguments

x

For as_neuro(), a niftiImage, internalImage, oro.nifti nifti object, file name or neuroim2 object. For as_nifti(), a NeuroVol or NeuroVec.

...

For as_neuro(), further arguments passed to read_image when x is a file name; otherwise unused.

label

For as_neuro(), an optional label for the result.

xform_code

The code written to sform_code and qform_code: 1 (scanner anatomical, the default), 2 (aligned to another image), 3 (Talairach) or 4 (MNI152). neuroim2 does not record which of these a space is, so say so here when it matters downstream.

reference

Ignored; present because RNifti::asNifti() has it.

Value

as_neuro() returns a DenseNeuroVol or DenseNeuroVec. as_nifti() returns a niftiImage.

Details

as_neuro() accepts

  • an RNifti niftiImage or internalImage, e.g. the result of RNifti::readNifti() or of an RNiftyReg registration;

  • an oro.nifti nifti object, e.g. the result of oro.nifti::readNIfTI(), neurobase::readnii() or an fslr command;

  • a file name, which is passed to read_image;

  • a neuroim2 object, which is returned unchanged.

A 3-D image becomes a DenseNeuroVol and a 4-D image a DenseNeuroVec. Trailing dimensions of extent 1 are dropped first, so a 4-D image with one volume becomes a volume.

The voxel-to-world affine is taken from RNifti::xform(), which applies the NIfTI rule: the sform if it is set, else the qform, else a scaling by the voxel sizes. RNifti and neuroim2 share one convention for it (zero-based voxel indices to RAS+ millimetres), so trans(as_neuro(img)) equals RNifti::xform(img) to the seven significant figures a NeuroSpace keeps. Data scaling (scl_slope, scl_inter) has already been applied by the package that read the image, so values carry over as they are.

as_nifti() returns an RNifti niftiImage holding the values of x as a dense array. The affine of x is written to both the sform and the qform, and the voxel sizes to pixdim. The qform can only describe a rotation with scaling, so for an affine with shear the qform is the closest such transform and the sform is the exact one; readers that follow the NIfTI rule use the sform. Any object with an as.array() method and a space can be converted, so sparse, clustered, memory-mapped and file-backed objects are read into memory by the call. A logical volume is stored as 0/1 integers.

Because RNifti::asNifti() is an S3 generic, asNifti(x) works on neuroim2 objects as well and gives the same result as as_nifti(x). To get an oro.nifti object, pass the result on: oro.nifti::nii2oro(as_nifti(x)).

Volume labels, NIfTI extensions and header fields other than the geometry are not carried across in either direction.

See also

read_image, write_vol, as_nifti_header

Examples

fname <- system.file("extdata", "mni_downsampled.nii.gz", package = "neuroim2")

# An image read by RNifti becomes a neuroim2 volume ...
img <- RNifti::readNifti(fname)
vol <- as_neuro(img)
all.equal(trans(vol), RNifti::xform(img), check.attributes = FALSE,
          tolerance = 1e-6)
#> [1] TRUE

# ... and a neuroim2 volume goes back, with its geometry
smoothed <- gaussian_blur(vol, as.mask(vol > 0), sigma = 2)
img2 <- as_nifti(smoothed)
RNifti::pixdim(img2)
#> [1] 4.02083 4.01754 4.02083
